summary: Confusing throttle accounting: short-lived token fan-out yields early 429s and inconsistent Retry-After headers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a pattern of early 429s when distributing a batch of short-lived API keys (one per worker) across ~1,200 parallel upload workers. Each worker uses a short-lived token minted by the customer's auth service (rotated every ~5 minutes). The customer is on a Dedicated pool and observes 429 throttles within 10–30s of starting a fan-out, even though aggregate token usage should be within tenant quota. Retry-After headers are inconsistent: some 429 responses include a short Retry-After (2s), others include none, and a few include large values (120s).

Impact:
- Upload jobs fail at scale with high retry churn, increasing latency and cost.
- Customer's canary warmups for batch jobs are intermittently failing which blocks deployments.
- Observed across multiple models (redwood-v1.3, gptx-open-7b) in us-east.

Environment:
- Customer: NimbusSearch Inc. (dedicated)
- Pool: dedicated-us-east-1a, Reserved capacity 12xA100 equivalent
- Client behavior: 1,200 short-lived keys minted via internal broker, each worker initiates 10 parallel streams to the streaming generation endpoint. Tokens rotate every 5 minutes.
- Time window of reports: 2026-03-09 22:00 — 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (repro harness provided by customer):
1) Mint N short-lived keys (N ~ 1,200) and distribute to parallel uploader workers.
2) Each worker opens 10 concurrent streaming sessions to /v1/stream?model=redwood-v1.3 and sends a short prompt (~30 tokens), repeating every 20s.
3) Observe 429 rate and Retry-After headers in responses within the first minute of fan-out.

Observed behavior:
- Rapid 429s with inconsistent Retry-After headers.
- Token accounting in internal dashboards shows tokens attributed to different token-buckets (per-key vs per-tenant) inconsistently.
- Some 429 responses are immediately followed by successful requests for the same token after 3–4s, others require much longer backoff.

Expected behavior:
- Throttles should be attributed to the tenant-wide token bucket when per-key limits are not configured, and Retry-After should reflect the same backoff policy consistently across edge proxies.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Reduce parallelism from 1,200 -> 300 short-lived tokens per fan-out and increase per-worker concurrency to keep throughput.
- Switch to longer-lived tokens (rotation every 30m) for bulk uploads.

Logs / response samples provided by customer:
- Sample 429 with small Retry-After: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 2
  X-RateLimit-Scope: tenant-token
  X-Request-Id: rwd-req-43a2
- Sample 429 w/o Retry-After: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  X-RateLimit-Scope: per-key
  X-Request-Id: rwd-req-54b9
- Sample immediate success after 429: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  X-Request-Id: rwd-req-54ba

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Short-lived keys are being mapped to per-key buckets at the edge because token-service metadata is missing or delayed, causing per-key buckets (which are small) to throttle even though tenant quota exists.
- Hypothesis B: Edge proxy cache TTL for token->tenant mapping is too short; on high-fanout we see cache misses and concurrent warmups causing inconsistent accounting across proxied hosts.
- Hypothesis C: A race in distributed rate-limiter where internal counters are incremented by health-checks/worker heartbeats leading to unexpected token consumption.
- Early checks: reproduced locally with smaller fan-out (300 tokens) when edge cache TTL set to 0s. With TTL=60s, behavior stabilizes.
- Dashboards referenced: /dashboards/tenant-rate-usage?tenant=nimbussearch, /dashboards/edge-cache-misses

Next steps planned:
- SRE to instrument token-service responses with cache-control and add debug logging for token->tenant resolution (PR suggested below).
- Patch edge-proxy to annotate 429 responses with canonical Retry-After calculated from tenant bucket when mapping is ambiguous.
- Run controlled ramp test with customer reducing parallelism and increasing token TTL to confirm hypothesis.
steps_to_reproduce: Mint ~1,200 short-lived keys and distribute to parallel workers
Each worker opens 10 concurrent streaming sessions to /v1/stream with redwood-v1.3
Observe 429s within first 60s of fan-out and capture response headers
observed_behavior: High-rate 429s with inconsistent Retry-After values; some tokens succeed immediately after a 429 while others remain blocked for long periods. Token accounting shows mixed attribution between per-key and tenant buckets.
expected_behavior: Rate-limiter should consistently attribute throttles to tenant-wide bucket unless explicit per-key quotas are configured. Retry-After should be present and consistent with the bucket state.
logs_and_samples: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests - Retry-After: 2 - X-RateLimit-Scope: tenant-token - X-Request-Id: rwd-req-43a2
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests - no Retry-After - X-RateLimit-Scope: per-key - X-Request-Id: rwd-req-54b9
HTTP/1.1 200 OK - immediate success after 429 - X-Request-Id: rwd-req-54ba
investigation_notes: Edge cache TTL set to 0s reproduces issue locally; TTL=60s stabilizes behavior
Token-service sometimes returns tenant info with 100–300ms delay under burst
Rate-limiter counters show spike from health-check probes on dedicated pool during fan-out windows
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer opened after observing repeatable failures in canary jobs. Provided initial repro harness and logs.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11: Assigned for investigation. Confirmed inconsistent X-RateLimit-Scope values in traces across edge hosts. Planning controlled ramp tests.
DevOps (customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed switching to longer-lived tokens dramatically reduced 429s; will stand by for controlled ramp test.
Marcus Lee (Edge team) 2026-03-12: Small change proposed to edge-proxy to prefer tenant-level Retry-After when mapping ambiguous, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4421
temporary_workaround: Recommend customers reduce fan-out concurrency, use longer-lived tokens for bulk uploads, or pre-warm edge cache by issuing a small set of tenant-scoped requests before large fan-outs.
resolution_notes: In progress: workarounds communicated. Edge team preparing a patch to improve Retry-After annotation and edge cache behavior. SRE to run controlled ramp with customer. Will update when PR lands and post-deploy validation passes.
follow_up_actions: Edge: annotate 429s with canonical tenant Retry-After when mapping ambiguous (PR #4421)
Auth/token-service: ensure token->tenant mapping includes cache-control header and minimize latency under burst
SRE: create automated ramp test harness for short-lived-key fan-outs and add dashboard for edge cache misses
